title: Jim Cramer Says Stay Long Airbnb Stock (ABNB) Despite Fee Concerns
detail:
Jim Cramer Says Stay Long Airbnb Stock (ABNB) Despite Fee Concerns
Syeda Seirut Javed
Fri, August 28, 2026 at 2:21 PM MDT 3 min read
ABNB
Trade Airbnb on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

A caller on the August 26 episode of Mad Money highlighted local neighbors abandoning Airbnb over a forthcoming change that shifts guest fees directly in listing prices. They asked if they should dump their 5% Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) holdings and invest in Toll Brothers. Jim Cramer replied:

Well, I do like Toll Brothers very much, but I have to tell you, I think you're an outlier. As I know, the Jersey beaches, they're always trying to figure out how to stop the party houses; I wouldn't worry. Internationally, Airbnb is smoking it. I say you stay long that stock.

Jim Cramer Says Williams-Sonoma (WSM) Selloff Was Wrong After Strong Earnings
Strong Results Support Cramer's Growth Argument

Airbnb, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:ABNB) second-quarter revenue rose 17% year over year to $3.6 billion, while gross booking value increased 16% to $27.2 billion and nights and seats booked grew 10% to 148.3 million. Net income reached $816 million, adjusted EBITDA rose 21% to $1.3 billion, and free cash flow was about $1.3 billion. Management raised its 2026 outlook to at least 15% revenue growth and an adjusted EBITDA margin of at least 35.5%.

International growth remains important to the thesis. Airbnb reported stronger growth across major markets, while hotel nights are growing about three times faster than its home business. Hotels still account for a single-digit percentage of total nights, but about 35% of first-time guests who book a hotel on Airbnb later return to book a home.

Management also reported a 16% year-over-year decline in customer-support costs per booking, helped by its AI assistant, which resolves nearly 45% of issues that begin with it without human intervention. However, the new 15.5% host-paid fee remains a risk because higher listing prices remains a potential host-retention risk.

Bear Case

The bigger risk is that Airbnb, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:ABNB) stock has already priced in much of the recent improvement. Shares closed at $188.07 on August 26, just below the $193.45 52-week high reached on August 24. At that price, it trades at roughly 35 to 36 times forward earnings, based on current market-data estimates. That valuation leaves less room for a slowdown in bookings, margins, or international demand. Furthermore, regulation adds another risk. Short-term-rental restrictions can reduce available listings in individual markets, while hotels and online travel agencies remain significant competitors.

Hedge Fund Ownership Fell, While Short Interest Remains Low

Institutional positioning provides a more cautious signal. According to Insider Monkey, 75 hedge funds held ABNB in the second quarter of 2026, down from 87 in the first quarter. Moreover, Insider Monkey's data shows that over the past few quarters, Harris Associates was the biggest hedge fund shareholder tracked by Insider Monkey with approximately 18.9 million shares in Q2. It is worth noting that short interest offers less evidence of bearish conviction. Multiple market data providers put short interest at roughly 3% of float, and that level indicates limited bearish positioning rather than aggressive speculative bearishness.

title: Palo Alto Stock Is Riding A Wave Of AI Fear, But What Happens Next?
detail:
Palo Alto Stock Is Riding A Wave Of AI Fear, But What Happens Next?
Trefis Team

Photo by TheDigitalArtist on Pixabay

Management raised the bar on its future, and after a moment of doubt, investors have been piling in ever since, forcing a critical question about how much momentum is left.

When Palo Alto raised its full-year revenue forecast back on June 2, you might have expected a pop in the stock. Instead, the market's immediate reaction was a 5.6% drop. It was a classic head-scratcher. The real story here isn't just that management is more optimistic; it's about why the market eventually agreed with them so forcefully, and whether that conviction is already fully priced in.

What Did the Market See on the Second Look?

The rally wasn't built on a single number. It was the breadth of the guidance lift that seems to have won investors over. Management didn't just nudge revenue; they raised targets for cash flow, operating margins, and earnings per share. Digging deeper, the company revealed its next-generation firewall bookings had risen nearly 40% year-over-year, the strongest hardware performance in a decade. In an environment where every company is scrambling to build out AI infrastructure, that kind of demand for the core network security hardware that inspects traffic is a powerful signal. It suggests the company is capturing a direct slice of the AI data center buildout.

Is This More Than Just a Hardware Boom?

A surge in hardware sales can be cyclical, but the company is making the case that this is part of a bigger, more durable shift. The company is pushing a "platformization" strategy, aiming to become the all-in-one security provider for its clients. It now counts roughly 2,280 of these deeply integrated customers. This isn't just about selling more firewalls; it's about locking in recurring revenue streams. For instance, its SASE business, which secures access for remote workforces and applications, saw its annual recurring revenue hit $1.6 billion, a 40% year-over-year jump.

This combination of a hot hardware cycle and a growing recurring software base is the one-two punch the market seems to be rewarding. The options market is certainly bracing for some action. Current pricing implies a 52% volatility for the company's shares, which is in the 85th percentile of its one-year history. In plain terms, traders are betting on an unusually large price swing around the next earnings report, scheduled for September 1.

After a big run-up, a company doesn't just have to meet a higher bar; it has to clear it convincingly to keep the momentum going. The market has bought the growth story, but that purchase comes with a ticket for a potentially bumpy ride. The company has successfully sold Wall Street on its role as the essential security layer for the AI revolution. The question now is whether it can deliver the flawless execution a stock priced for near-perfection demands.

title: Bernstein Revamps Airbnb Stock Target For Rest of Year

Bernstein Revamps Airbnb Stock Target For Rest of Year
Moz Farooque ACCA
Mon, August 24, 2026 at 12:43 PM MDT 2 min read
ABNB

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Bernstein SocGen Group analyst Richard Clarke just delivered one of Wall Street's more aggressive Airbnb (NASDAQ:ABNB) calls, lifting his price target to $217 from $168 while keeping an Outperform rating. The 29% target increase implies roughly 16% upside from Airbnb's recent $187.30 price, with Clarke arguing that accelerating bookings and strong margins have pushed the company to a clear inflection point.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Sign with ABNB.

Is ABNB fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The call comes after Airbnb posted one of its strongest quarters in years. Second-quarter revenue climbed 17% to $3.6 billion, gross booking value increased 16% to $27.2 billion, and Nights and Seats Booked rose 10%, accelerating from the first quarter. Adjusted EBITDA jumped 21% to $1.3 billion, while margin expanded to 35%.

Clarke sees the booking trajectory as particularly important. Management is guiding toward a fifth consecutive quarter of approximately 10% or higher night growth, suggesting Airbnb may be sustaining a faster growth rate than investors currently expect.

That creates the valuation argument behind Bernstein's upgrade. Clarke estimates Airbnb's current share price embeds medium-term revenue growth of only about 10.5% to 11%. He believes sustained double-digit revenue growth, incremental margin gains and continued buybacks could support approximately 20% annual earnings per share growth.

New businesses could add another layer. Clarke highlighted AI-driven search, dynamic pricing, loyalty programs and sponsored listings as potential long-term growth drivers, including opportunities to improve conversion and create new advertising-style revenue streams.

Investors Takeaway

The biggest test is whether booking growth stays around double digits as comparisons become tougher. Investors should watch Nights and Seats Booked, revenue growth, adjusted EBITDA margins and gross booking value.

Airbnb already showed meaningful acceleration in Q2, but a stock trading near its 52-week high has less room for disappointment.

If bookings remain above 10% growth and new monetization initiatives begin lifting revenue faster than expected, Bernstein's $217 target becomes easier to justify. A slowdown in travel demand or weaker margins would challenge the inflection point thesis.

Target Rallies On Earnings Gain, Outlook Optimism

title: Eli Lilly Stock Raised Its Forecast, So Why Is The Market Shrugging?
detail:
Eli Lilly Stock Raised Its Forecast, So Why Is The Market Shrugging?

Management is betting on a bigger year than ever, but investors seem to be waiting for a catch.

When a company with a $1.12 trillion market cap tells you it expects to pull in an extra few billion dollars, you listen. On Aug 5, 2026, the company did just that, significantly raising its full-year 2026 revenue guidance. And the market's reaction? A polite nod. The stock gained +4.9% on earnings day and has added another +7.5% since, with the market steadily validating management's raised outlook rather than pushing back on it.

How Much Bigger Is The Bet?

The guidance update came with key moving parts: management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance by 3% and lifted its performance margin target by 2 full percentage points, even while modestly trimming its full-year EPS guidance. This comes on the heels of a quarter where revenue grew 48% year-over-year, driven by the blockbuster performance of its incretin drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound. The company is signaling that its commercial engine, already running at full throttle, has found another gear. For a company of this scale, adding billions to the top-line forecast is a significant statement of confidence.

Has The Easy Money Already Been Made?

Perhaps the market's hesitation is understandable. After a stock has climbed 79% in a single year, it's fair to ask how much good news is already baked into the price. Investors are now looking past the headline numbers for cracks in the story. Some analysts have pointed to the launch of the oral drug Foundayo as being "slower than anticipated," while others noted that the company's own guidance implies a potential deceleration in growth in the back half of the year. When you're priced for perfection, any hint of a slowdown gets magnified.

The market is actively debating what level of future growth is truly baked into Lilly's multiple—a question explored in our recent breakdown of what the stock's valuation actually implies. It's the classic standoff: the company delivered the numbers, but the market is questioning if it can keep delivering at the same pace.

Is The Market Bracing For A Shock, Or A Snooze?

Here's where it gets interesting. If investors were truly nervous about the company hitting this higher bar, you'd expect to see that anxiety reflected in the options market. But it's not. The stock's implied volatility sits at 32%, which is in the lower 27th percentile of its one-year range. Traders aren't betting on a big swing in either direction. Instead of pricing in risk, they're pricing in relative calm. What does this market calm truly signify? It's a bet that the drama is over for now.

Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) did everything bulls wanted. The company's Q2 revenue, reported on August 6, 2026, highlighted a 17% rise in revenue to $3.6 billion, a 16% increase in gross booking value to $27.2 billion, and a net income of $816 million. Its management lifted full-year guidance on both revenue and margins, reflecting the AI story in its numbers. The stock ran to a four-year high near $184, up 32% year to date. Then, on August 11, Phillip Securities's Paul Chew downgraded the stock to Reduce even as he raised his target to $158 — still about 14% below the price. This contradiction gives a whole new story.

Airbnb Expands Travel Platform with Airport Pickups, Grocery Delivery, and Car Rentals
The Quarter Was Real. That's the Point.

Under the microscope, there is nothing to nitpick in the print. But that is exactly why the downgrade matters. The AI payoff is tangible.  An AI assistant now resolves nearly 45% of issues without human intervention. Subsequently, the customer-support cost per booking fell 16%. Additionally, the pace of product shipping in the first half ran roughly 80% ahead of the same period last year while cutting concept-to-launch time by up to 60%. Adjusted EBITDA margin guidance moved up to approximately 35.5%. With such a great quarter, an already expensive stock is made more expensive.

30x Is the Whole Debate

Airbnb trades near 30.9 times earnings, above its own two-year-plus-one-standard-deviation of 29.6x, and on a trailing basis closer to 41.7x. Let's compare this against the peers. Yahoo Finance currently puts Booking Holdings at roughly 20 times forward earnings and Expedia near 17 times, versus about 35 times for Airbnb. It means that Airbnb premium is substantial even with less than half of Booking's scale. Meanwhile, the premium-assumed growth is cooling at the edges. Nights and Seats Booked grew 10%, trailing the 17% revenue gain, and take rate was flat at 13.2%. Instead of an upside, the reacceleration and the AI payoff are becoming assumptions baked into the price.

Everyone's Already Long

Positioning confirms the market concentration on the stock. Insider Monkey database recorded 87 funds holding ownership in the first quarter of 2026 – up from 80 in Q4 2025. Short interest sits at just 3.39% of float as of mid-August. Q3 revenue guidance of $4.69 billion to $4.77 billion provides the next test.

Bottom Line

Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB)'s second quarter is excellent. But the downgrade is a tell that easy money has been made. With earnings two or three times its competitors and with its long side already packed, the risk-reward is flipping. Do not chase the four-year high. Use the core metrics like take rates and room-night growth against the Q3 guide of $4.69–4.77 billion to determine if the stock really deserves the premium.
